payload.purpose_context: Before the docsite cuts over from DocFX to doc-kitty, the real GitHub Pages service must be shown to serve the doc-kitty build's redirect stubs, pages and directory URLs. An operator-dispatched canary in the deploy workflow builds the site through the one shared build definition, deploys it, probes a ledger-derived sample of URL classes over HTTP, and always redeploys DocFX. The probe is the logic the post-cutover smoketest (#2361) reuses.
payload.purpose_tldr: A dispatched canary deploys the doc-kitty build to Pages, probes the live D-13 URL classes, then restores DocFX (#6938 PR A)

payload.question: Who starts the canary, when, and what must it prove?

payload.final_answer: The operator dispatches docs-pages.yml from main with canary=true in an announced window with docs merges frozen. The run builds the doc-kitty site through the shared docs-site-build.yml (D-11), deploys it to Pages, probes a ledger-derived sample of D-13 URL classes on https://docs.spec-kitty.ai, then always rebuilds and redeploys DocFX and fails the run if the probe failed. Answered from the operator brief for #6938 PR A.

payload.question: Which URL classes does the probe check, and how is the sample chosen?

payload.final_answer: Derived from the committed ledgers (url-baseline.txt, moves.yaml, legacy-redirects.json), never a hand list: one .html key to its own page, one moved-chain key, one live dir/index.html (rule 3), one dir/README.html, one directory URL, plus the site root, /llms.txt and one retired /kitty-specs/ route expected 404. Stubs must name the map's target and the target must serve 200. Answered from the operator brief.

The non-canary push and dispatch path stays DocFX behaviour; deploy stays main-only and core-repository-only; the Pages probe-then-configure job stays; the canary never leaves the doc-kitty site live (DocFX always redeployed); the cutover is a later PR B and not done here. Answered from the operator brief.

payload.question: How does the canary order its jobs so DocFX is always restored and the default path stays unchanged?

payload.final_answer: The DocFX build job is untouched and builds in parallel; the canary publishes only after both the shared doc-kitty build and the DocFX build succeeded; the probe runs after the canary publish; the existing deploy job waits on the probe and runs on !cancelled() || canary, so it republishes DocFX whatever the probe said, while its default-path semantics are equivalent. Brief-derived engineering decision.

reason: Review passed (reviewer-renata). Push path: deploy needs [build, canary-probe]; with the skipped canary-probe, '!cancelled()' lets deploy run only after a successful DocFX build, matching GitHub's documented rule (a skipped need skips the job unless its if: holds a status function). The model applies implicit success() over the ancestors, which matches that rule. Cancellation: 'inputs.canary' runs the DocFX restore even on a cancelled canary run, still gated on build success; canary-deploy cannot have run without a successful build, so production is never left on the canary with no restore. pages concurrency (cancel-in-progress false) is safe both ways. Artifacts: github-pages-canary vs the default github-pages. Permissions are per job. SHAs checked with git ls-remote: deploy-pages 368f825 = v5.0.1, upload-pages-artifact fc324d3 = v5.0.0, checkout 08c6903 = v5.0.0. The fork guard is intact. The ADR change is an appended amendment only. Red commit 599f78f5d: 19 failed. tests/ci + release + arch gates 3289 passed. tests/docs 2338 passed. actionlint and ruff are clean. The _gh_expr.py:45 mypy error is identical on origin/main. Low: (1) the modified DocFX deploy job still uses tag-pinned deploy-pages@v5 (pre-existing; FR-006 keeps the default path, so pin it in a follow-up); (2) the canary probe URL is a literal, which could instead be canary-deploy's page_url output; (3) cancellation is not modelled in the tests, which is acceptable given the reasoning above; (4) a few assertions restate YAML (permissions dicts, the with: block).
